title: Integrability of a Gaussian profile composition
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a finite measure space and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, with $f(x)\in[0,1]$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Then the composition of $f$ with the Gaussian profile that equals $\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$ and $0$ otherwise is integrable with respect to $\mu$.
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. If $\mu$ is a finite measure on a measurable space $\Omega$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $f(x)\in[0,1]$ for every $x$, then $\overline I\circ f$ is $\mu$-integrable.
